title: A negative search can incorrectly become a birth boundary
finding: The guide suggests that repeated non-listings locate a likely start and tells researchers to stop at the first non-listing. Estimates can omit, aggregate, rename or relocate a unit.
action: Record the actual searched scope, terminology and outcome; continue relevant checkpoints and alternate ministries. Never derive a founding/end date from a negative search.

title: Current ministry lineages are unreliable historical search boundaries
finding: The Climate Action Secretariat’s suggested 2010 ministry disagrees with the 2010 Environment vote. The Fire Commissioner is named under CAWS in 2002.
action: Retain leads as explicitly unverified. Store the document’s exact ministry label and observation date; search across contemporary rosters.

title: Discovery leads mix abolition, continuation and a still-operating service
finding: Industry Training Appeal Board is legally continued under a new name; BC Ambulance Service’s current page describes it operating under BCEHS. These are unsafe gone-body examples, not proven errors in an unseen gone database.
action: Require explicit cessation evidence. A rename normally stays one identity; a different successor is linked separately; a surviving nested service is not gone.

title: The export loses provenance for inherited claims
finding: All 175 event rows contain only date/type/title; none include source or locator. Selected start dates and sightings are also flattened scalars.
action: Export full dated claims, claim IDs, locators, precision, alternative claims and editorial decisions, or include the exact upstream research files at a pinned revision.

title: Dated does not mean the start has been reviewed
finding: Six C-only records still say not_researched; two C-only records explicitly require reconciliation. Date presence determines routing more strongly than evidence maturity.
action: Track research completeness and reconciliation independently of timeline priority. Existing date claims must remain reviewable.

title: Retrospective testimony is being confused with contemporary observation
location: README.md: Track A; selected held names/first_observed rows
finding: A later history statement can support existed-by testimony but is not necessarily a founding statement or a contemporaneous sighting. Several held observations originate in later annual reports/about pages.
action: Store claim effective date, source publication/observation date, date precision and testimony type separately. Do not turn all “since” statements into establishment claims.

title: First-sighting work is not yet connected to timeline behaviour
finding: The guide explicitly says the diagram does not use first_observed to draw historical bodies. Collecting data alone will not resolve disappearance.
action: Implement and test an evidence-aware resolver with historical names and parents, unknown-start labels and non-continuity safeguards. Do not claim the renderer is fixed by this packet.

title: Budget placement is not a universal organizational-parent relation
finding: Only part_of/subsidiary_of are offered, while the queue contains independent bodies, programmes, accounts, facilities and projects. Budget chapters also group functions for appropriation purposes.
action: Preserve budget placement as its own fact. Expand typed relationships only with schema/runtime support and appropriate evidence, rather than forcing a misleading parent.

title: The handoff is not reproducible against an identified code revision
finding: The archive lacks the build/merge code and several linked research files. The public main package inspected has differently named scripts and no research:merge or build:government alias.
action: Pin the upstream commit and include the complete dependency set, schemas, generator and tests. Do not run unsupported merge commands against an unidentified checkout.

title: The batch handback instruction contradicts its own skeleton
location: All 23 batch Markdown files, handback paragraph
finding: Every batch says one JSON object per body, but its skeleton and README specify one object per batch containing records.
action: Correct the generated boilerplate and its generator. The included documentation patch fixes the exported copies only.

title: Succession does not establish an exclusive end date
finding: The parenthetical describes the end as the day the successor began. Distinct bodies can overlap; transferred functions do not by themselves prove closure.
action: Require independent cessation evidence and an explicit interval convention. Keep cessation, transfer and successor commencement as separate claims.

title: A 2026-survivor queue is not a historical government census
location: README.md: current-source collection and Track D
finding: The 238-item inventory starts with present-day bodies. It cannot discover every abolished, absorbed or otherwise absent historical unit by following survivors backward.
action: Add period-specific roster extraction, then resolve entities and relations. Keep discovered candidates separate until identity and evidence checks pass.

title: Some selected events exceed the certainty of their descriptions
location: Held histories: Timber Sales, Wildfire, Corrections, CRT, Parks
finding: The snapshot contains bounded name changes, competing date descriptions, function origins and repeated milestones. Source-free flattening makes automatic selection unsafe.
action: Restore claim provenance; use bounded temporal claims and milestone types; do not assign an exact day to an observation interval or erase disagreements.

title: A fiscal document is not a year-long organization chart
finding: Earlier-year comparison columns are restated to the current presentation. Cabinet changes within one year also make a ministry label year-dependent.
action: Use the actual document and as-of date. Do not read a restated prior-year column as historical parentage, or a checkpoint year as a full documented span.

title: INDEX timeline counts are upstream assertions, not reproducible here
finding: The reported counts are 23 for 2010 and 8 for 2000. A simple selected-start-year filter yields 25 and 13. This is not proof of a renderer bug: parent/lifecycle rules are absent.
action: Reproduce the actual resolver at the pinned revision and explain every inclusion/exclusion. Keep archive counts distinct from renderer regression tests.

title: Record kinds mix organizations with programmes and delivery objects
location: sub-agencies.json: kind (82 programmes plus other kinds)
finding: A general-purpose public-sector atlas can include programmes and assets, but a uniform agency/daughter node implies relationships that evidence may not support.
action: Define display semantics by entity kind and relationship; do not remove programmes solely because they are not legal persons.
